correctness.rationale: In the subdivision-incidence graph, distinct selected originals witness each other at distance two, a selected original and inserted vertex witness one another only if incident, and distinct inserted vertices witness one another exactly when their parent edges share an endpoint. For a fixed set B of omitted originals, all pairs inside B must be selected to dominate their inserted vertices. A crossing edge is required to dominate a lone omitted original (b=1), to witness the sole forced B-edge (b=2), or to witness a lone selected original (a=1). For b≥3 all forced inserted vertices already have witnesses, and every optional inserted vertex has a selected original endpoint. Thus the free within-A choices and the cross-edge exclusion give exactly the two cases of Q and the displayed polynomial. The minimum-size contributions from b=0,1,2 are 1, n(n−1), and n(n−1)(n−2); from b=3 it is binom(n,3), except when n=4 and the lone selected original needs an extra cross edge. For b≥4 the forced size bound is n+b(b−3)/2>n. This includes n=3 with b=3 and no selected originals. A separate definition-level enumeration matched every coefficient for n=3,4,5,6, with minima 14,37,91,171 at degrees 3,4,5,6.
residual_risks: The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed. The independent replay tests only n≤6; the general proof is the classification by omitted originals. No claim extends to other base graphs or partial subdivisions.

value.rationale: The cardinality polynomial of a natural infinite subdivision family strengthens both the known optimum value and the independent-set counts. The formula gives all coefficients and resolves the exact prevalence of minimum sets, including the n=4 exception and the large contribution of adjacent selected vertices. The small enumeration is not the contribution; the structural characterization supports uniform exact counting.
